summary: Adam Air was a privately owned Indonesian airline. It was based in West Jakarta. It flew to over 20 domestic cities. It also flew to Penang and Singapore. It offered low fares with on-board meals. Before the Flight 574 crash, it was Indonesia's fastest-growing low-cost carrier. Agung Laksono and Sandra Ang founded it in 2002. Laksono was Speaker of the House of Representatives. Ang's son, Adam Suherman, became chief executive. Flights began on 19 December 2003. Its safety record was heavily criticised. Pilots reported deliberate breaches of safety regulations. They said unairworthy planes flew for months. Critics said it used political connections to sidestep regulators. The Flight 574 crash in January 2007 ended foreign investment interest. In 2008, investors holding 50 percent pulled out over safety. More than half the fleet was seized after defaulted payments. The government suspended its operating certificate on 18 March 2008. It revoked the certificate on 18 June 2008. The airline then ceased operations. Police named owner Sandra Ang an embezzlement suspect. Reported losses were about US$210 million.
